description: The worked example (pick-exception report) through interview engine v2: each user message and the model outputs the engine asks for that turn, in call order. Code decides everything else.

steps.user: /intake-kit:intake I need a report of short picks by shift and picker so the shift leads can target retraining instead of guessing.

output.title: Daily pick-exception report
output.trigger_quote: I need a report of short picks by shift and picker

output.question: When you see that report, what will you do differently?

steps.user: So I know who to pull for retraining that week. Right now I build it in Excel every Monday and it eats my whole Monday morning.

output.value: Decide who to pull for retraining each week
output.quote: So I know who to pull for retraining that week

output.question: Who touches this report, from the person who builds it to the people who use it?

steps.user: I build it, the three shift leads use it on Tuesday, and the DC manager signs off on retraining.

output.value: The supervisor builds it; three shift leads use it; the DC manager signs off
output.quote: I build it, the three shift leads use it on Tuesday, and the DC manager signs off on retraining

output.question: How will you know it's working, and what is the current way costing you?

steps.user: Today it takes about four hours every Monday. If the leads pick the right people, short picks per picker should drop within a month.

output.value: Four hours every Monday now; short picks per picker should drop within a month
output.quote: Today it takes about four hours every Monday

output.question: Where does the data come from, and which copy do you trust?

steps.user: It all comes out of the WMS pick confirmations. We've got read access to the reporting copy. No customer data or pricing, just orders, locations and badge numbers.

output.value: WMS pick confirmations, read from the reporting copy; no customer or pricing data
output.quote: It all comes out of the WMS pick confirmations

output.question: Which screens or systems do you open for it, and is anything changing in the next six months?

steps.user: Just the WMS reporting copy and Excel. Nothing is changing on the WMS this year.

output.value: The WMS reporting copy and Excel; no changes this year
output.quote: Just the WMS reporting copy and Excel. Nothing is changing on the WMS this year.

output.question: Does it have to be ready by a certain time, or does anyone outside your team require it?

steps.user: It needs to be there by 7am when I walk in. Nobody outside the team requires it.

output.value: Ready by 7am daily; no outside requirement
output.quote: It needs to be there by 7am when I walk in

output.question: When a count is wrong today, who catches it?

steps.user: I guess the shift lead would catch it.

output.quote: I guess the shift lead would catch it.

output.question: Tell me about the last time a count was wrong. Who caught it, and what happened?

steps.user: Honestly I don't remember one. If a count looks wrong the shift lead checks it with me before pulling anyone, and if the counts stopped matching the WMS I'd go back to the Excel sheet.

output.value: The shift lead checks a wrong-looking count with the supervisor; if counts stop matching the WMS, back to the Excel sheet
output.quote: If a count looks wrong the shift lead checks it with me before pulling anyone

output.question: When you count a short pick, what's in and what's out?

steps.user: Short picks and wrong-location scans, not the cancelled lines. Count them per picker, per shift, per day.

output.value: Short picks and wrong-location scans, excluding cancelled lines
output.quote: Short picks and wrong-location scans, not the cancelled lines

output.question: Is there a report today that's close to this? What's wrong with it?

steps.user: The WMS dashboard only gives me the total for the building, nothing by picker.

output.value: The WMS dashboard shows building totals only
output.quote: The WMS dashboard only gives me the total for the building

output.question: Do you still build that Monday Excel sheet by hand today? When did you last do it?

steps.user: Yes, I built it last Monday. If I had the daily report every morning I'd stop doing the Monday thing.

output.value: The Monday Excel sheet, built by hand weekly

output.question: Roughly how long does the Monday sheet take, and how often do you do it?

steps.user: About four hours, once a week, every Monday morning.

output.value: About four hours once a week
output.quote: About four hours, once a week

prose.text: Retraining is chosen by guesswork because short picks aren't visible by picker and shift.
The supervisor builds a Monday Excel sheet from the WMS export, which takes about four hours.
A daily report of short picks and wrong-location scans per picker, per shift, ready by 7am.
Cancelled lines; deciding who gets retrained.
A shift lead checks a count with the supervisor before pulling anyone.

acceptance.given: a shift with short picks and wrong-location scans
acceptance.then: each picker's count for that shift is shown, excluding cancelled lines

acceptance.given: the counts stop matching the WMS
acceptance.then: it says so instead of showing the counts

guardrails.text: Stop using it for retraining if the counts don't match the WMS.
Go back to the Monday Excel sheet.
A shift lead checks a count with the supervisor before pulling anyone.

output.reflect_back_text: A daily short-pick and wrong-location report per picker and shift, ready by 7am, so shift leads can choose who to retrain.
